newsitem.title: INDIA: India castor prices gain, but overseas buying low.
newsitem.headline: India castor prices gain, but overseas buying low.

text.p: Indian castorseed June delivery prices on Friday rose to 1,186/1,187 rupees per quintal from 1,180/1,181 rupees despite low overseas buying, dealers said.
Overseas buying was low but limited arrivals of castorseed at producing centres as well as reports of an uptrend in the world market triggered fresh bull buying, one dealer said.
Short-covering by bear operators also kept prices firm.
Castor arrivals at producing centres remained low on account of the ongoing strike by transport operators across India.
Groundnut oil rose by 1/2 rupees at 254/255 rupees per 10 kg on a shortage of ready stock following the absence of fresh arrivals due to the strike.
"Imported palm oil was steady at 285/286 rupees per 10 kg on the absence of fresh arrivals from the port to the market," one importer said.

"One steamer carrying about 3,000 tonnes of imported palm oil is waiting for unloading at the Bombay port but the transport strike has delayed the unloading as well as delivery to the market," he added.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil was steady at 540/545 rupees per 15 kg. -- Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
